items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to pediatric day-respite center
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3459

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public health law, in relation
to pediatric day-respite center

 PURPOSE :

To authorize Daystar for Medically Fragile Children, Inc., to be
licensed as New York state's first and only Pediatric Day-Respite
Center, delivering comprehensive family support services, educational
enrichment programs, developmental services, and pediatric healthcare
services to serve the needs of medically fragile and terminally ill
children and their families.

 SUMMARY :

Section 1 of this bill would amend the public health law by adding a
new section 2803-ff.

Section 2 of this section would make the bill take effect in the
hundred eightieth day after it shall have become a law.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Daystar serves as a unique program model for the State of New York by
providing coordinated case management services, educational programs,
specialized developmental services and daily pediatric skilled nursing
for up to forty children under age six who have a broad scope of
intensive healthcare needs. While Daystar is dually authorized and
regulated by OPWDD and OCFS, there remain critical gaps in
center-based, step-down services for children with special healthcare
and developmental needs. Unlike other states that recognize
comprehensive Pediatric Day-Respite Center models as an effective
management tool for high-needs populations, NYS lacks a formal
mechanism within DOH to license and authorize direct healthcare
services provided at Daystar.

By establishing Daystar as a Pediatric Day Respite Center, it will
save New York State significant funding as Daystar costs ten times
less than what NYS spends on pediatric hospital services and four
times less than what NYS spends on private duty nursing. In addition,
the program facilitates hospital discharge of sub-acute, medically
complex children and minimizes readmissions; avoids preventable
emergency room visits; provides economic independence; and allows
family members to maintain their employment.

Daystar provides a highly efficient framework for delivering
comprehensive, coordinated services to families who are struggling to
transition their medically fragile child from hospital to home. If
enacted this program will establish New York State as a vanguard for
comprehensive care for medically fragile children.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016 passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect in the hundred eightieth day after it shall
have become a law.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 190
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 3459-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the social services law and the public health law,
      in relation to pediatric day-respite centers and care"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Social Services Law and  the  Public  Health
Law  to:  (1)  establish  pediatric  day-respite  centers  which deliver
comprehensive family support services; and (2)  authorize  reimbursement
for  pediatric  day-respite  care  as new Medicaid and Child Health Plus
(CHIP) services. The bill would also require the Commissioner of  Health
to  promulgate  regulations to implement procedures and requirements for
an entity to qualify as a pediatric day-respite center.

  While I fully support the intent of the bill to provide respite  care,
I  cannot  support  the  bill  as  drafted.  First, respite services are
already provided to children at home through private duty nursing  under
the  Medicaid  program,  as  well  as under the Home and Community-Based
Services Waiver operated by the Office  for  People  with  Developmental
Disabilities.  Second,  this  bill would require the establishment of an
entirely new licensure and certification process, as well as correspond-
ing surveillance and compliance review  by  the  Department  of  Health,
without any funding to create and sustain such an infrastructure.
 
  Third,  this  bill  would  result in an expansion of Medicaid and CHIP
services, without going through the Evidence Based Benefit Review  Advi-
sory   Committee  (EBBRAC)  vetting  process,  created  to  make  sound,
evidence-based determinations on the efficacy of a treatment. As some of
the benefits proposed in this bill have not yet been  evaluated  by  the
EBBRAC, the bill would circumvent this established vetting process.
 
  Finally,  as  the bill would expand services reimbursed under Medicaid
and CHIP, it would result in an increased, unbudgeted cost to the  Medi-
caid  program  outside  the  budget  process. At a time when the Federal
government has enacted, and is threatening additional, devastating  cuts
to  the  State's  health care system, it would be irresponsible to incur
such unbudgeted costs at this time. For these reasons  I  am  forced  to
veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
